mainTopic: A נזיר who discovers his impurity after his term, and the rules of a hidden body (טומאת התהום) and floating טומאה
overview: The amud opens by answering an earlier question: a נזיר became טמא during his term but found out only after it ended. רבא proves from the משנה that he still cancels (סותר) his days. The משנה says 'in either case he cancels,' and that would be obvious if he found out during the term. The גמרא then asks whether he cancels everything or only seven days. It shows that this question fits רבי אליעזר's view: one could follow when he became טמא, or when he found out. It answers from the same משנה. The משנה does not divide the cases, so he cancels seven. Next, a ברייתא discusses someone who finds a body lying across a road. He is טמא for תרומה but טהור for a נזיר and the קרבן פסח, and the ברייתא narrows this step by step: whether there was room to pass, whether the body was whole, walking versus riding, and a known versus a hidden טומאה (טומאת התהום). It defines טומאת התהום as a body nobody in the world knew of, gives examples, and limits the rule to a dead body. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה's floating body. It teaches that floating טומאה does not make things טמא in the case of a שרץ, citing a ברייתא where רבי שמעון distinguishes between water in a vessel and water in the ground.

steps.title: רבא brings a proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה: if he found out before shaving, he cancels his days in either case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: If he found out before he shaved, he cancels his days in either case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer the earlier question by quoting a line from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the נזיר discovered his impurity before shaving, he cancels (סותר) his days no matter what. רבא will show that this line answers the question about finding out after the term ended.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
He shaved: the haircut that ends the נזירות
Cancels: the earlier days of נזירות stop counting
Either way; in both cases

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
If before he shaved —
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה: he found out about the impurity before he did his final shaving.

phrases.english: in either case, he negates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised before this section, about finding out after the term ended.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a נזיר who found out about his impurity only after the term ended still cancels his days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'אם עד שלא גילח בין כך ובין כך סותר.'

steps.title: What case is the משנה describing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when exactly the נזיר found out about his impurity in this משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to pin down the exact case in the משנה. This sets up the next step, where the proof is completed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the משנה is talking about finding out after the term. So the גמרא first asks which case the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up the analysis of רבא's quoted source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did the נזיר in the משנה find out during the term or after it?

steps.title: It must mean he found out after the term
steps.stepSummary: If he found out during the term, the ruling would be obvious. So the משנה must mean after the term, and he still cancels.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it became known to him during the full term, does that need to be said? Rather, it must mean after the full term. Conclude from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רבא's proof. A משנה would not teach something obvious, so the case must be finding out after the term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he found out while still in his term, of course he cancels, since he has not finished yet. The משנה would not need to say that. So it must mean he found out after the term (מלאת), and he still cancels. This answers the original question.

keyTerms.meaning: The completion of the נזירות term
Does it need to be said? Meaning, it is too obvious to teach
Rather, is it not...? It must be the other case
Learn from it; the proof is complete

steps.whatToRemember: According to the משנה, even when the impurity is discovered only after the term ends, the נזיר still cancels his days.

phrases.english: If it became known to him during the full term —
phrases.notes: מְלֹאת is the completion of the days he vowed to be a נזיר.

phrases.english: need it be said?
Rather, is it not after the full term?
Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what is the case' question and completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That finding out after the term still causes cancellation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה does not teach the obvious, so the case must be after the term.

steps.title: Follow-up: all the days or only seven?
steps.stepSummary: Even now that we know he cancels, the גמרא asks whether he cancels all his days or only seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you can still ask: does he cancel all of it, or does he cancel seven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new follow-up question about the same case: how much does he cancel?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know he cancels his days. The new question is how many. Either he cancels the whole נזירות, or he cancels only seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: And you can still ask: a question remains open
He cancels everything; the whole term must restart
He cancels only seven days

phrases.english: And you can still raise the question:
Does he negate all of it, or does he negate seven?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that he does cancel, and asks how much.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the cancellation covers the whole term or only seven days.

steps.title: Whose view could this question even fit?
steps.stepSummary: The question seems to have no room. רבנן would clearly say everything, and רבי אליעזר would clearly say seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? If you say according to the רבנן, it is obvious he cancels all of it. And if according to רבי אליעזר, anything after the full term cancels seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the follow-up question. Each opinion seems to already have a clear answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן hold that even impurity after the term cancels everything, so for them there is nothing to ask. רבי אליעזר holds that impurity after the term cancels only seven, so for him the answer also seems clear. The question looks pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
If you say...
It is obvious
A תנא who holds that impurity after the term cancels only seven days

phrases.english: According to whom?
If we say according to the Rabbis —
phrases.notes: This refers to their earlier argument with רבי אליעזר about becoming טמא after the term.

phrases.english: it is obvious that he negates all of it.
And if according to Rabbi Eliezer:
anything after the full term, he negates seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question in step 4 has any room.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under each opinion the answer is already clear, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: It fits רבי אליעזר: he became impure before the term ended
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's 'seven' may apply only when he became טמא after the term. Here he became טמא before it ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: that rule applies when he became impure after the full term, but this one became impure before the full term.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the question. The question can be asked according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's rule of seven might be only for someone who actually became טמא after the term. In our case the impurity happened during the term, so perhaps it cancels everything.

keyTerms.meaning: He could tell you: the one asking defends himself
These words apply only when...
He became impure

phrases.english: He could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, כִּי נִטְמָא אַחַר מְלֹאת,
phrases.english: This applies when he became impure after the full term,
but this one is before the full term.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by placing the question within רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבי אליעזר's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's 'seven' covers every case connected to after the term.
steps.terutzMaskana: His 'seven' may apply only when the impurity itself happened after the term.

steps.title: Or does the late discovery make it count as after the term?
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the question: since he found out after the term, maybe the case counts as after the term, and he cancels only seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is different here, since the knowledge came after the full term?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the other side of the follow-up question, so both sides are now clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possibilities. One is to follow when he became טמא, which was during the term, so he cancels all. The other is to follow when he found out, which was after the term, so he cancels seven.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps: the other side of a question
It is different here
Knowledge; the moment he found out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two moments in this case. He became טמא during the term, but he found out after the term. The whole question is which moment counts.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא דִּידִיעָה אַחַר מְלֹאת הִיא?
phrases.english: it is different here, since the knowledge is after the full term?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question, after step 6 showed the first side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the time of finding out decide the case, or the time of becoming טמא?

steps.title: Resolved from the משנה: no distinction
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'in either case he cancels' and does not split the cases. So the ruling is the same, seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from it: it teaches 'in either case he cancels,' and it does not distinguish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the follow-up from the same משנה. The משנה gives one ruling for both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses one wording, 'in either case he cancels,' without dividing between finding out during the term and after it. That suggests one uniform rule: he cancels only seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: And from it: we answer from the same source
It teaches
It does not distinguish between the cases

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not divide the cases, so finding out after the term is treated the same way: the נזיר cancels seven days.

phrases.english: And from it:

phrases.aramaic: קָתָנֵי בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ סוֹתֵר,
phrases.english: it teaches "in either case he negates,"
and it does not distinguish.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִינַּהּ: קָתָנֵי בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ סוֹתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in steps 4 through 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה does not divide the cases, so the ruling is uniform: seven days.

steps.title: A body lying across a road
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that someone who finds a dead body lying across a road is טמא for תרומה but טהור for נזיר and קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If someone finds a dead body lying across the width of a road, for תרומה he is impure. But for a נזיר and for someone bringing the קרבן פסח, he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. The case is a dead body lying across a road that a person walked on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same person gets two different rulings depending on what is at stake. For תרומה he is treated as טמא. For נזיר and פסח he is treated as טהור, because this kind of unknown, hidden טומאה is treated leniently for them, like the earlier discussion on the דף.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught. This opens a ברייתא.
A dead body lying there
Across the whole width of the road
The holy portion given to a כהן. It may only be eaten in purity.
Someone bringing the קרבן פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the base rule. The rest of the ברייתא keeps narrowing it.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who finds a dead body lying
across the width of a road,
for תרומה, he is impure,
but for a נזיר and one bringing the פסח, he is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמּוֹצֵא מֵת מוּטָל לְרׇחְבָּהּ שֶׁל דֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא after the discussion of whether he cancels all his days or seven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a body across the road: טמא for תרומה, טהור for נזיר and פסח.

steps.title: Only when there was no room to pass
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the ruling for תרומה. It applies only when there was no room to get by the body. If there was room, he is טהור even for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When he had no room to pass by. But if he had room to pass by, he is pure even for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a first limit to its own rule. It explains exactly when the passerby is טמא for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the body blocked the whole road, he surely passed over it, so for תרומה he is טמא. If there was room to walk around it, maybe he never passed over it. A doubt about טומאה in a public area is ruled טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? This introduces a limit on a rule.
Room to pass by

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ruling that he is טמא for תרומה.

phrases.english: Where he has no room to pass by,
but if he has room to pass by,
even for תרומה he is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לַעֲבוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the תרומה ruling of step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If there was room to pass by, he is טהור even for תרומה.

steps.title: A whole body versus a body in pieces
steps.stepSummary: The ruling applies only to a whole body. If it was in pieces, he may have walked between them, so he is טהור. In a grave, though, the grave joins the pieces, so he is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When he found it whole. But if it was broken or taken apart, then even if there was no room to pass, we worry that maybe he passed between the pieces. And in a grave, even if it is broken and taken apart, he is impure, because the grave joins it together.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second limit. It only applies when the body was whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a body in pieces, even a blocked road leaves gaps, so there is a real chance he stepped between them. A grave is different. The whole grave counts as one unit of טומאה, so passing over any part of it makes him טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Whole, in one piece
Broken or taken apart into pieces
We worry about, we take into account
The grave joins it together into one unit

steps.confusionAlert: Here the worry, חיישינן, leads to a lenient ruling. We take seriously the chance that he passed between the pieces, and that chance makes him טהור.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
Where he found it whole.
But if it was broken or taken apart,
even if there is no room to pass by,
we worry that maybe he passed between the pieces.
And in a grave, even if broken and taken apart,
he is impure, because the grave joins it together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to the ruling, about a whole body versus pieces.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A body in pieces leaves him טהור, since he may have passed between the pieces. In a grave he is טמא, since the grave joins the pieces.

steps.title: Walking versus carrying a load or riding
steps.stepSummary: The leniency for a body in pieces applies only to someone walking on foot. Someone carrying a load or riding an animal surely touched, moved, or passed over a piece, so he is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? About someone walking on his feet. But if he was carrying a load or riding, he is impure. Someone walking on his feet can manage not to touch it, not to move it, and not to pass over it. Someone carrying a load or riding cannot avoid touching it, moving it, or passing over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds its last limit and explains the reason. The leniency of walking between the pieces only works for someone on foot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person on foot can step carefully between the pieces. A person weighed down by a load cannot walk straight, and a rider sits high on an animal. So they will surely become טמא in one of three ways: touching, moving, or being over the body.

keyTerms.meaning: Walking on his own feet
Carrying a load, or riding an animal
Moves it, which is a way to become טמא even without touching
Is over it, under one covering with the body (אוהל)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא keeps narrowing its rule. He is טמא for תרומה only if the road was fully blocked. That holds only if the body was whole, or if it was in a grave. For a body in pieces, he is טהור only if he walked on foot.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: This refers to the lenient ruling about a body in pieces.

phrases.english: About someone walking on his feet.
But if he is carrying a load or riding, he is impure.
Because someone walking on his feet
can manage not to touch it
and not to move it and not to pass over it.
Someone carrying a load or riding
cannot avoid touching it
or moving it or passing over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the lenient ruling for a body in pieces from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency for a body in pieces applies only to someone walking. Someone carrying a load or riding is טמא.

steps.title: The leniency applies only to an unknown, hidden impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the leniency for נזיר and קרבן פסח applies only to טומאת התהום. If the טומאה was known, all three are טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? With an impurity of the depths. But with a known impurity, all three of them are טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits its earlier ruling. A נזיר and someone bringing a קרבן פסח are treated as טהור only if the dead body was a hidden, unknown טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the person is טהור for נזיר and פסח. Now we learn this applies only to טומאת התהום, a body nobody knew was there. If the body was known to others, even if not to him, he is טמא for all three, including נזיר and פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the depths: a source of impurity that nobody knew about
A known source of impurity
All three of them

steps.confusionAlert: "Known" does not mean the person himself knew. It is enough that someone else knew about the body.
steps.whyThisMatters: This limit explains why נזיר and פסח get a leniency at all. It works only for a truly hidden טומאה.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: "These words" means the earlier ruling that he is טהור for נזיר and קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: With an impurity of the depths.
But with a known impurity,
all three of them are impure.
phrases.notes: The three are נזיר, קרבן פסח, and תרומה from step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit to the ברייתא from step 9, this time on the leniency for נזיר and פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency for נזיר and פסח applies only to טומאת התהום. With a known טומאה, all three are טמא.

steps.title: Definition: no one in the world knew of it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines טומאת התהום as a body nobody in the world knew about. If even one person anywhere knew, it is not טומאת התהום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What counts as an impurity of the depths? Any body that not even one person, even at the end of the world, knows about. If one person at the end of the world knows about it, it is not an impurity of the depths.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks and answers its own question to define the term it just used. It sets a very strict test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question here is not a challenge. It simply sets up a definition. The test is whether anyone at all knew of the body. Even one person far away is enough to make it a known טומאה, and then the leniency is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Knows of it, is aware of it
At the end of the world, meaning anywhere at all, even very far away

phrases.english: And which is an impurity of the depths?
Any that not even one person knows of,
even at the end of the world.
If one person at the end of the world knows of it,
this is not an impurity of the depths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term טומאת התהום introduced in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טומאת התהום is a body that no one in the world knew about. If even one person knew, it does not count.

steps.title: Examples: hidden in straw and pebbles versus water, darkness, and rock clefts
steps.stepSummary: A body buried in straw or pebbles counts as טומאת התהום. A body in water, in a dark place, or in rock clefts does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the body was buried in straw or pebbles, it is an impurity of the depths. In water, in darkness, or in the clefts of rocks, it is not an impurity of the depths.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives real-life examples to show how the definition works. It judges by where the body was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A body covered by straw or pebbles was likely never seen by anyone, so it counts as hidden. Water, dark places, and rock clefts are places people rarely go, yet a body there is likely to be noticed over time. So we assume someone may have known of it, and it is not טומאת התהום.

keyTerms.meaning: Straw
Pebbles, small stones
Darkness, a dark place
Clefts or cracks in the rocks

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume a hard-to-reach place makes a body hidden. Water and rock clefts seem hidden, but the ברייתא says they do not count.

phrases.english: If it was buried in straw or in pebbles,
this is an impurity of the depths.
In water and in darkness
and in the clefts of the rocks,
this is not an impurity of the depths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the definition from step 14 to specific places where a body might be found.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A body buried in straw or pebbles is טומאת התהום. A body in water, darkness, or rock clefts is not.

steps.title: The rule applies only to a dead body
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes by saying the leniency of טומאת התהום applies only to a מת, not to other sources of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they said the rule of an impurity of the depths only for a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with one last limit. The leniency of a hidden טומאה applies only when the source is a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the earlier details about hidden impurity apply only to a מת. Other sources of טומאה do not get this leniency, even if they were hidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead body
Only, alone

steps.whatToRemember: The leniency for נזיר and קרבן פסח works only when two things are true. First, the טומאה is טומאת התהום, meaning nobody in the world knew of it. Second, the source is a dead body (מת).

phrases.english: And they did not say the rule of an impurity of the depths
except for a dead body alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם אֶלָּא לְמֵת בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא by limiting the whole טומאת התהום leniency to a מת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The leniency of טומאת התהום applies only to a dead body, not to other sources of impurity.

steps.title: Floating טומאה does not make things impure in the case of a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of the floating body. It then teaches that floating טומאה does not make things טמא when the source is a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught: 'How? If he went down.' A floating impurity does not make things impure when it comes to a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a נזיר who went down to immerse and found a body floating. It then adds a limit: floating טומאה does not cause טומאה in the case of a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a floating מת makes the נזיר טמא. The גמרא now teaches that floating טומאה is different when the source is a שרץ. In that case, a ספק caused by something floating stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How? If he went down.' These are the opening words of the משנה's case being discussed
Floating, meaning a source of טומאה floating on top of water
A dead creeping creature, which is a source of טומאה
Makes something impure

phrases.english: 'How? If he went down.'
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words about a נזיר who went down to immerse in a cave and found a body floating at its opening.

phrases.english: A floating impurity does not make things impure
in the case of a שרץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a new line in the משנה, the case of the floating body, after finishing the discussion of טומאת התהום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Floating טומאה does not cause טומאה when the source is a שרץ.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that doubtful floating טומאה is pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as its source. When there is a doubt about touching floating טומאה, the item is טהור, whether the water is in a vessel or in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: In a case of doubtful impurity that was floating, whether in a vessel or in the ground, the item is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what it just said about floating טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that when it is unclear whether something touched floating טומאה, the ruling is טהור. This applies whether the water is held in a vessel or lies in the ground, like a well. So floating טומאה does not create the usual stringency of a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
A case where it is unclear whether something became impure
Vessels. Here it means water held in a vessel
The ground. Here it means water in the ground, like a well or pit
Pure

phrases.english: As it is taught: A doubtful impurity that is floating,
whether in vessels or in the ground, is pure.
phrases.notes: He means floating in water that sits in a vessel, or in water in the ground, like a well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that floating טומאה does not make things impure in the case of a שרץ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that a doubtful floating טומאה is טהור, whether in vessels or in the ground.

steps.title: רבי שמעון makes a distinction between a vessel and the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees in part. He says floating טומאה in a vessel is טמא, and floating טומאה in the ground is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: In vessels it is impure. In the ground it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the same ברייתא, רבי שמעון gives a different view from the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that floating טומאה in water in the ground is טהור. They disagree only about water in a vessel. The first opinion says it is טהור, and רבי שמעון says it is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא
Impure

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that doubtful floating טומאה in water in the ground is טהור. רבי שמעון rules it טמא only when the water is in a vessel.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
In vessels, it is impure;
in the ground, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the disagreeing view inside the same ברייתא quoted in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: doubtful floating טומאה in a vessel is טמא, and in the ground it is טהור.
